description:

I hiked 'Mount Martial' and sailed through the Beagle Channel to two islands. On one of them, there's 'El Faro del Fin del Mundo', where a colony of sea lions lives; there's also a penguin colony.

From my experience, everyone should visit Ushuaia. What do you think? Have you heard of Ushuaia?

title: Learn About Board Games in Spanish
description:
There are many varieties of board games. We can play them with friends, family, or for competition.

The board game industry is very large in Europe and the United States. The world of board games is also vast as they have many subgenres. Some are suitable for all audiences, while others have restrictions.

Card games have been popular for many centuries and, in fact, they are the most popular type of board game. In Argentina, "Truco" is the most popular card game.

There are even "party games." These usually have few components and are easy to explain. This is motivated by the little space they require.

Deduction games are another genre and perhaps the most interesting because of everything they involve.

title: Argentinian Daily Menú - Español Al Vuelo S02 x Ep 11
description:
In general, in our country Argentina, people eat four meals a day.

Unlike other countries, Argentina has a "sweet" and lighter breakfast.

Lunch isn’t very heavy either, but it’s savory. It’s usually something quick.

The afternoon snack, or merienda, is important, as it’s typically enjoyed around 4 or 5 PM. In Buenos Aires, restaurants aren’t open at that time. Instead, people gather in cafés, sipping coffee and eating sandwiches.

Dinner is the heaviest meal of the day. It’s when we eat more abundantly.

What really sets us apart is the timing—while the dishes are similar to those in other countries, in Argentina, dinner starts at 8 PM at the earliest, and that’s considered early!

What are mealtimes like in your country? Tell us in the comments if they’re very different from those in Argentina!
